original_test_intent: Determine whether the authorized Chassis resource advertises a documented Chassis.Reset capability and what its supported reset types are, without invoking any reset; the source cannot safely define a direct request to the action target.
original_method: Keep the case blocked, read only the parent Chassis resource's `Actions` metadata if needed, and require the firmware/vendor action specification plus a corrected testcase before any action-target method or payload is proposed.
manual_activity: The Redfish/firmware owner must decide whether the case is parent-resource capability discovery or a disruptive reset invocation and supply the exact supported verb, target, ResetType set, expected response, impact and recovery contract.
required_inputs: Target firmware and Redfish/vendor action specification
Documented Chassis.Reset target and allowable methods
If invocation is intended: exact ResetType, outage scope, active-workload gate, OOB recovery and acceptance
Trusted least-privilege credential and certificate policy
safety_requirements: Do not GET the action target without documented support
Do not change GET to POST
Do not normalize the malformed path into an executable request
No reset, reboot or power transition
agent_execution_scope: Read only the parent Chassis resource if approved
Compare advertised target and allowable values to vendor specification
Prove no POST, ResetType, reset or power transition occurred
engineer_actions: Correct the testcase and provide authoritative action semantics
Approve a separate reset safety/recovery plan if invocation is intended

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It must not run: the source path is malformed, GET on an action target has no documented expected contract, ipmitool is unrelated, and silently changing to POST could reset or power-cycle the selected chassis.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: BLOCKED. At most, securely GET the authorized parent Chassis resource and inspect its `Actions` object; do not request the Chassis.Reset target or send any reset payload until the testcase and vendor contract are corrected and separately approved.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Chassis.Reset name and 15/10 timing are retained only as unresolved source facts; member, verb, payload, reset type and expected response are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Separate capability discovery from invocation: first validate advertised Actions metadata against the firmware specification, then create a distinct, fully approved reset testcase only if actual invocation is intended.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Prevents an action URI from being treated as a readable resource and prevents a guessed verb correction from triggering a reset.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Parent-resource metadata can prove the capability is advertised but cannot prove action authorization, invocation, transition or recovery. Those require a separate disruptive test.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Any attempted correction to POST may reboot, power-cycle or interrupt workloads. A GET failure such as 404/405 would reveal the source defect, not validate reset capability.

project_override_considerations: No client or vendor tool may invoke reset under this record. A vendor SDK can only read the parent resource's Actions metadata while blocked; invocation requires a new approved contract and confirmation gate.
expected_evidence: Authorized Chassis identity and target firmware
Secure parent Chassis HTTP response and redacted Actions metadata
Advertised reset target and allowable-values comparison
Preserved BMC/SEL/OS and workload/power state evidence

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The testcase calls itself a GET of Chassis.Reset but points directly at an action target using GET, includes a malformed path spacing and defines no readable action-resource response. If it actually intends reset invocation, the required method/payload/criteria are absent and cannot be inferred safely.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Available source and reference material cannot establish a safe supported GET contract for the action target or distinguish capability discovery from reset invocation. Changing the method could disrupt the platform, so authoritative semantic correction is required.

review_improvement: Stops the ambiguous action-target request, confines permitted work to parent metadata and specifies the semantic and reset-safety artifacts needed for a corrected testcase.
independent_technical_reasoning: Redfish actions are advertised from a resource's Actions object and are normally invoked with a state-changing request and action-specific parameters; the target is not automatically a GET-readable resource. Here the path itself is malformed and no expected representation exists. Treating GET failure as success would not prove the capability, while changing to POST would authorize a potentially disruptive reset absent any ResetType, workload gate or recovery plan. Therefore the execution semantics are irreducibly blocked, although parent metadata can be collected safely as diagnostic evidence.
